items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Bess; the mention is made by the interviewer who states 'Bess just satisfies that need for them.'

ctx.x: No, I haven't been able to figure that out. I know more than that. The people over there seem to appreciate more than the people here, you know. People here just want to get, well, I don't want to say what's in my mind. If they can't get a drink or be out with a girlfriend, it is assuming they don't come in, you know. That's not really interested in the music. You just want to go someplace, you know. Look how people go for jazz here. They love it. But now you let a jazz band go down an auditorium or the super…

I think it's a question of authenticity and I think that the Europeans have a great appreciation for American culture. And the Americans have a great appreciation for popular culture. So, you know, it's a question of, they want to know what, they want to know about the history of New Orleans music, all the way from traditional jazz and of course blues. And the tremendous fascination with all kinds of artists that are totally obscured here. So, Bess just satisfies that need for them. And he represents New Orleans…

Yeah, that's certainly true. Because when I was in England, people always asking me about it. They found out I was from New Orleans. They always ask me about it. Do you mind it when people like, talk a lot? When you play, I've noticed this not so much when you play because people dance a lot. But I've been in certain clubs that won't come mention here where people, as you say, they're there for, to drink or, I don't know, impress whoever they're with. And they don't really listen to musicians. Does all that noise…
